title: License + provenance + output-license + PII/aggregation gate checklist
context: open-data-explainers publishes derivatives — aggregations, summaries, and tools built from open datasets. This means the output license is not automatically the same as the input license. Share-alike sources (ODbL/OSM, some GTFS feeds) propagate their terms to derived databases; GTFS feed licenses vary per agency; SDSS/Gaia releases may be non-commercial. A committed, reviewable gate checklist is the hard gate that every module must pass before publishing, ensuring no share-alike violation, no person-level PII output, and correct attribution.
objective: Define and document the license + provenance + output-license + PII/aggregation gate checklist that every explainer module must pass before publishing, including share-alike propagation rules, per-feed GTFS gating, SDSS/Gaia NC handling, and aggregate-only PII rules.
acceptanceCriteria: Records per source: license id + URL + committed text snapshot (copy + SHA-256 + Wayback), permitsDerivative:true with cited clause, and the resolved output license of our derivative. Missing/unparseable evidence = FLAG/EXCLUDE; never default-allow.

Encodes share-alike propagation (ODbL derived databases must be released ODbL; OSM attribution required) and per-feed GTFS gating (exclude restrictive/no-derivative/unclear feeds) and SDSS/Gaia NC handling (carry NC label or exclude; never launder NC into permissive output).

PII/aggregation rule: only aggregate or already-de-identified data; for person-derived sources (STATS19) require aggregate-only output, a minimum cell count k >= 5 per geo/temporal bin, and a geo-precision limit; never person-level output; never de-anonymise.
Produces a committed, reviewable PASS/FLAG/EXCLUDE artifact per source/region that the License reviewer signs off.
Reviewed and approved by the named License reviewer (reviewers-001) before the M0 pilot submits for review.
resources: PLAN.md — Data, licensing & compliance section (per-source output-license matrix)
PLAN.md — Quality, review & risk gates section
output: A committed gate checklist document and machine-readable schema (e.g. gate-checklist.md + gate-schema.json) defining the PASS/FLAG/EXCLUDE criteria per source, ready to be applied as a non-skippable gate for every explainer module.
